note: The main banks were taken as Serbia's three largest by assets, a choice from general knowledge (no central bank or association ranking was read in this pass): Banca Intesa, OTP banka Srbija and UniCredit Bank Srbija. Banca Intesa: its conditions of approval for the Visa Gold (enclosure 103, from 1 September 2023), Mastercard Gold (enclosure 93, from 1 January 2025) and Mastercard Platinum (enclosure 113, from 11 June 2026) credit cards, read 2026-10-30. Each bears a fixed nominal rate on spending in dinars, written (15.62%, 13.12% and 7.93% a year); the lower rates on spending in foreign currency (12.60%, 10.85%, 4.62%) aren't written. Their annual membership for the primary card is 6,000, 6,000 and 16,800 dinars; the Mastercard Gold's waiver and the Platinum's 25% or 30% reductions for holders of the bank's Magnifica or Hit Plus accounts aren't written, the game not holding those accounts. The monthly obligation is at least 5% of the total spent, at least 100 dinars (5 euros), plus interest and due fees. Cash at Banca Intesa's ATMs costs 3%, at least 90 dinars, on the Gold cards; the Platinum's sheet as read states none. Delay bears the statutory default rate where higher, which varies and isn't written. The Mastercard Standard is issued only within a payment account package, which the game doesn't hold, and isn't written. OTP banka Srbija's and UniCredit Bank Srbija's card terms weren't reached in this pass (UniCredit's sites elsewhere answered with an IP check).
